intent_snapshot.goal: Run an Initiative-shaped loop work item as one v3 batch through startLanes with entry_kind initiative, retain_branch, parent_relayed and final_verification.required true from the project batch verification commands, record its batch_id on WorkItem.binding, re-enter advanceLanes for that batch on every tick (adopting an orphaned active batch by task lookup), and emit one E13 at batch completion, replacing the S1 lane_initiative_entry_pending refusal, per D2 of docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-DEC-A1, BR-DEC-A5; meet D2.1-D2.3 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-daemon-drive-pr.test.ts, tests/lane-sessions.test.ts. Done looks like: an Initiative drive with a fake executor provider and scrubbed HERDR_* writes one v3 record with entry_kind initiative, retain_branch, parent_relayed and final_verification.required true carrying the configured commands. Negative: with no configured final verification commands it refuses final_verification_required and writes no record; without a usable provider it refuses lane_session_unavailable; single-task drives still use required false.

Source BR-DEC-A1; meet D2.4-D2.5 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-leader-dispatch.test.ts. Done looks like: binding.batch_id is written after the first drive; three later ticks call advanceLanes with that id and create no second batch record; a batch started before a simulated crash prevented the binding write is adopted by task lookup instead of duplicated; batch completion yields exactly one E13. Negative: a terminal or missing recorded batch clears batch_id before a new startLanes; the lane_initiative_entry_pending refusal no longer exists.

intent_snapshot.scope_size_reason: The Initiative entry kind, the dispatcher input, the WorkItem binding and the per-tick re-entry form one start-then-advance contract; splitting them would leave a batch that starts but is never advanced.

attestations.summary: Initiative entry now authorizes one v3 batch (retain_branch, parent_relayed, required final verification) via dispatchInitiativeDrive, re-enters/adopts via resolveInitiativeBatchId and binding.batch_id, refuses final_verification_required/lane_session_unavailable/rejected without records, settles once (one E13), and removes lane_initiative_entry_pending; antigravity runtime mirrors are byte-identical; blast radius medium: batch_state.ts entry-kind persistence (initiative maps to absent plan_source), drive_dispatcher.ts, agent_handlers.ts, WorkItem.binding shape.

advisory_findings.summary: The three-later-ticks case is asserted only through resolveInitiativeBatchId and a fake driveInitiative; no test observes that dispatchInitiativeDrive actually calls advanceLanes (not startLanes) for the recorded id.

evidence.trigger: recorded active batch id on WorkItem.binding → dispatchInitiativeDrive advance branch is not observed by any test; a regression to startLanes would only be caught indirectly

advisory_findings.summary: Adoption by task lookup accepts any active v3 batch containing a slice task, including a single_task batch for that slice; advancing it with entry_kind initiative would then refuse on entry-kind mismatch rather than being ignored.

evidence.trigger: an active single_task Lane batch exists for one slice task and binding.batch_id is null → resolveInitiativeBatchId adopts it and the Initiative drive refuses instead of starting its own batch
